channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Taliban Chief of Staff Claims Anti-Taliban Fighters Are Not Afghan
item.description: Taliban Chief of Army Staff Fasihuddin Fitrat alleged that members of anti-Taliban fronts are not Afghan and their activities are staged. He accused Pakistan of ordering and supporting these groups to destabilize Afghanistan.

item.title: Paraguay's President impeached and arrested amid Ueno Bank crisis
item.description: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and arrested following a crisis at Ueno Bank. He is suspected of abuse of trust and using his position for personal gain. The bank's collapse led to millions losing access to their accounts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Human Dignity and Health in Healthcare Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev highlighted the nation's commitment to human dignity, life, and health in a congratulatory message to medical workers. Healthcare funding has increased sevenfold to 49 trillion soums, reflecting a state policy prioritizing citizens' well-being. Modern technologies and a national system for early disease detection have been implemented.

item.title: Azerbaijan Marks Victory Day, Commemorating Liberation of Shusha
item.description: Azerbaijan celebrates Victory Day on November 8, commemorating the 2020 liberation of Shusha, a pivotal event in the Second Karabakh War. This day signifies national pride and historical justice for Azerbaijanis. It also prompts international reflection on past lessons and future peace prospects in the region.

item.title: Kazakhstan Minister Visits University After Name Change
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Science and Higher Education, Sayasat Nurbek, visited Omir Innovation University in Almaty, previously named after Dinmukhamed Kunaev. He announced the university's new name and delivered a lecture to students.

item.title: Last Active Glacier in Austrian Alps Loses Active Status Due to Heat
item.description: The Schwarzmilzferner glacier in the Austrian Alps has lost its active status and stopped moving due to record summer heat in Europe. Its thickness decreased by four meters, and its volume roughly halved.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims for 100% Machine Cotton Harvesting by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to harvest 100% of its cotton mechanically by 2027, according to Agriculture Minister Ibrohim Abdurahmonov. In 2026, 75-80% of the cotton harvest is expected to be machine-picked, with full mechanization in Sirdaryo and Jizzakh regions. Small plots and areas inaccessible to machines will be converted to other crops.

item.title: Kyrgyz President instructs to include border fencing with Kazakhstan in 2027 plan
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered the inclusion of engineering border fencing with Kazakhstan into the 2027 plan. This directive came during a meeting where residents raised concerns about livestock crossing the border due to the lack of fences. Kazakhstan has already installed fences on its side.

item.title: SMS Remains Vital for Business Communications and National Security in Kazakhstan
item.description: Despite the rise of messengers, SMS is still the most reliable method for identity and transaction verification in Kazakhstan. Banks, marketplaces, and government platforms use it due to its universal accessibility and independence from internet quality. The market is shifting towards service-oriented SMS, including OTP codes and transactional notifications.

item.title: Who is Responsible for the Accidental Death During Bishkek's Green Construction Project?
item.description: A crane operator died at the 'Bishkek Green Construction' municipal enterprise during tree removal. His wife claims safety rules were violated, leaving seven children orphaned. The enterprise formed a commission and decided to pay partial compensation. The widow is distressed by the lack of a formal apology and the company's response.

item.title: Former President of FC Kyzylzhar, Grigory Loriya, Wanted for Embezzlement and Tax Evasion
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency has issued a wanted notice for Grigory Loriya, former president of FC Kyzylzhar. He is suspected of embezzlement and tax evasion. Loriya failed to appear for questioning and a court hearing regarding pre-trial detention. The investigation is ongoing, with details withheld for investigative purposes.

item.title: Afghanistan Among World's Five Most Climate-Vulnerable Nations
item.description: Afghanistan ranks among the five countries most vulnerable to climate change impacts, despite minimal contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions. The head of the National Environmental Protection Agency stated this at a conference in Kabul, warning the country could be third most vulnerable if comprehensive global research is conducted. Media's role in reporting climate change impacts was also highlighted.

item.title: UNICEF Reports Rising Child Malnutrition and Food Insecurity in Afghanistan
item.description: UNICEF has reported an increase in child malnutrition and food insecurity across Afghanistan. The agency's findings indicate a worsening situation for the country's youngest and most vulnerable populations. Specific details on the extent and causes of the rise were not provided in the initial report, but the trend highlights significant humanitarian challenges.

item.title: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan Sign Trade Deals Exceeding $151 Million
item.description: Private sector representatives from Afghanistan and Uzbekistan have signed dozens of trade agreements totaling over $151 million during a business meeting in Kabul. This initiative aims to expand economic cooperation and strengthen bilateral trade ties, with total bilateral trade now exceeding $1.8 billion.

item.title: Iran Executes Three Men Accused of Involvement in Anti-Government Protests
item.description: Iran has executed three men convicted of involvement in armed attacks during January's anti-government protests. State media reported they carried out operations on behalf of the United States and Israel. The judiciary stated they used firearms and explosives, causing power outages. Their assets were confiscated, and other defendants received prison sentences.

item.title: Two Oil Tankers Damaged by Mines in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Two oil tankers were damaged by mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Tasnim, citing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy. Both vessels caught fire after colliding with mines while attempting to pass through a restricted route. The UAE National Guard reported rescuing 22 individuals from a burning cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 300 People Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 79 families, totaling 335 people, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan. Returns occurred through various border crossings, including Torkham, Spin Boldak, Silk Bridge, and Islam Qala. The UNHCR reported nearly 1.29 million Afghan migrants returned from Iran and Pakistan by the end of September.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Urged to Investigate Investors in Araltuz Salt Company
item.description: Workers have appealed to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to launch an independent investigation into the operations of Araltuz, a salt production company. Allegations include aggressive, irrational extraction of salt reserves, disregard for environmental norms, and low wages. The appeal highlights concerns about the future depletion of salt resources due to current mining practices.

item.title: Man Sentenced to Six Years for Attempting to Sell 100kg of Marijuana in Kazakhstan
item.description: A 43-year-old man from Shu city has been sentenced to six years in prison for attempting to sell 100 kilograms of marijuana in Aktobe for 13 million tenge. He claimed to have found the drugs by the roadside and decided to sell them to cover debts. The buyer turned out to be an officer from the National Security Committee.

item.title: Israeli President Assigns Opposition Leader Gadi Eisenkot Mandate to Form Government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has announced he will give opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a new government. This decision follows consultations with parties participating in last week's parliamentary elections. Neither bloc secured the necessary 61 seats for a majority, presenting a challenge for both Eisenkot and rival Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: Doctor Honored for Saving Passenger's Life on Tashkent-Seoul Flight
item.description: Dr. Hasan Komilov was awarded the "Guardian of Public Health" badge for saving a passenger's life on a Tashkent-Seoul flight. The incident occurred on flight HY511, where Dr. Komilov provided emergency medical assistance to a woman in shock. His timely intervention helped stabilize the patient.

item.title: Unidentified Gunmen Kill 25-Year-Old Man in Afghanistan's Sar-e Pol Province
item.description: Local sources in Sar-e Pol Province reported that a 25-year-old man named Nawidullah was killed by unidentified gunmen in Sancharak District. The incident occurred early Sunday morning in Taghai Khwaja village. This event adds to the ongoing security incidents and killings in parts of Afghanistan.

item.title: Magnitude 3.7 Earthquake Recorded in Southern Kyrgyzstan on November 8
item.description: An earthquake with a magnitude of 3.7 occurred in southern Kyrgyzstan on the morning of November 8, 2026, at 05:14. The tremors were felt with an intensity of 3 points in the village of Bor-Döbö, Osh region. The epicenter was located 5 km southeast of Bor-Döbö at a depth of 15 km. This region has experienced previous seismic activity.

item.title: 2026-27 El Niño Event: Implications for Afghanistan's Climate Future Explained
item.description: Afghanistan is experiencing one of the strongest El Niño events in decades, influencing rainfall, snow, drought, and flood patterns. This article explains El Niño, its strength, affected regions in Afghanistan, associated opportunities, and risks for the general public, farmers, herders, and decision-makers.

item.title: UN Warns Hundreds of Health Facilities in Afghanistan May Close Due to Funding Cuts
item.description: The United Nations has warned that approximately 700 health facilities in Afghanistan could close or face financial difficulties this year due to declining international aid. The UN's humanitarian coordinator stated that aid has decreased significantly, impacting the operation of primary health services. This situation exacerbates existing pressures from returning migrants.

item.title: UNHCR: Nearly 1.29 Million Afghan Migrants Returned from Iran and Pakistan by September End
item.description: The UNHCR reported that nearly 1.29 million Afghan migrants returned from Iran and Pakistan by the end of September, with approximately 43 percent being deported. The agency provided cash assistance to over 202,000 asylum-seekers and returnees in border areas, along with grants for vulnerable families and individuals needing special support.

item.title: World Bank Reports Fourfold Decrease in Kazakhstan's Poverty Rate Over 20 Years
item.description: The World Bank reports that Kazakhstan's poverty rate has decreased fourfold over the past two decades. The proportion of the population earning above the poverty line has increased from 81.8% in 2006 to 95.1% currently. Income inequality has also reduced, with the Gini index falling to 29 points in 2024. The bank attributes this improvement primarily to rising labor incomes across all regions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Capable of Exploiting Own Mineral Resources 100%, Says President
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that Kyrgyzstan has the capability to fully exploit its own mineral resources. He emphasized that the country possesses sufficient specialists, experience, and opportunities for this. Japarov highlighted the significant increase in revenue from the "Altynken" enterprise since 2022 and noted that several mines previously under foreign control are now being operated domestically.

item.title: Afghanistan Requires a Strong, Modern, and Independent Army, States Defence Chief
item.description: Afghanistan's Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces, Fasihuddin Fitrat, stated the need for a strong, professionally trained, and well-equipped army to safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He emphasized that military strength is crucial for preserving independence and defending against internal and external threats, not for aggression or expansion. Fitrat also criticized the former Afghan National Defence and Security Forces for their reliance on foreign support.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Full Closure of Dolpran Mine Amid Resident Concerns
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered the complete closure of the Dolpran mine in the Chon-Kemin district if local residents oppose its operation and the state has no stake. A resident had appealed to the president, stating that mine operations were rendering 4,000 hectares of pasture unusable. State authorities confirmed the mine's license had been suspended.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Reviews Socio-Economic Development in Chuy Region
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov visited the Chuy region to review socio-economic development, implemented projects, and industrial growth. In Kara-Balta, seven new enterprises created 560 jobs, including metallurgy and textile firms. The region also saw the construction of social facilities and road improvements. Modern irrigation methods are being actively introduced in the Jayyl district.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Invest up to 1.4 Trillion Tenge in New 'Semei' SEZ Projects
item.description: Up to 1.4 trillion tenge will be invested in projects for the new special economic zone (SEZ) named 'Semei' in Kazakhstan. This initiative aims to foster economic development and attract investment within the designated zone.

item.title: Saudi Aramco Facility in Riyadh Targeted in Attack, Minor Damage Reported
item.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy confirmed an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was attacked. The ministry stated that shrapnel caused minor damage and there were no casualties. Houthi rebels have previously targeted Saudi oil facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Identify New Directions for Cooperation
item.description: During Tajik President Emomali Rahmon's official visit to Kazakhstan, key agreements were reached to strengthen bilateral cooperation. Priorities include expanding trade-economic ties, attracting investment, and developing partnerships in industry, agriculture, and transport-logistics. The goal is to increase bilateral trade to $2 billion.

item.title: Relatives of Doctor Sentenced to Three Years Appeal to President for Pardon
item.description: Relatives of Dr. Nasira Beishebaeva, a nephrologist sentenced to three years in prison, have appealed to President Sadyr Japarov for a pardon. The president indicated during a meeting with residents that assistance would be provided. The Bishkek City Court had previously overturned a lower court's probation decision.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Illegal land transfer causes over $1 million in state damages
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan's Aksy district, officials illegally transferred 7.74 hectares of land between 2021 and 2024. The Prosecutor General's Office estimates state damages at 91.3 million soms ($1.05 million). A criminal case for abuse of power has been opened as investigations into the unlawful land alienation continue.

item.title: Ukraine: Over 600,000 people without power after Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region
item.description: Russian forces launched a massive strike on infrastructure in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, damaging key energy facilities. Over 600,000 residents in Pavlohrad, Samara, Kamianske, Dnipro districts, and Dnipro city lost power. Hospitals and critical facilities switched to generators. Four people were injured in Poltava.

item.title: Paraguayan President Impeached and Placed Under House Arrest Amidst Bank Crisis
item.description: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest following the collapse of the Ueno bank. The crisis led to millions of clients losing access to their funds. Authorities are investigating the bank's lending practices and its ties to the country's elite.

item.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Gadi Eisenkot Receives Mandate to Form New Government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has granted Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition "Yashar!" party and former IDF Chief of Staff, the mandate to form a new government. Eisenkot secured 67 Knesset member recommendations, surpassing incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's 46.

item.title: Iran's Naval Commander Warns of Severe Repercussions for Any Future Attacks
item.description: Iran's naval commander, Mohsen Razzaqi, stated that any new attack on the country would incur a heavy cost. He emphasized the high level of coordination among Iran's armed forces and highlighted the importance of naval capabilities and geographical position in the nation's defense strategy. Senior officials also issued fresh threats of retaliation against the United States.
